title: Long MU — Q3 FY2026 Beat-and-Raise Event; NVDA Annual Meeting Same Day
entry: Enter $137–145 (MU at ~$143 going into the June 24 earnings event). Scale: 1/3 position immediately at current levels ($137–143); add another 1/3 only if DXY closes below 99.00 on Monday June 22 (regime gate confirmed); hold final 1/3 in reserve for any post-earnings pullback to $138–142 if the report delivers a beat but the stock fades intraday on profit-taking. Do NOT initiate above $148 — at that level pre-earnings premium is excessive relative to the $155 Target 1. If Monday June 22 DXY fails to clear 99.00, keep the position at 1/3 and reduce stop risk accordingly.
stop_loss: $128 daily close (~9.5% below $141.5 midpoint) — implies MU Q3 revenue or gross margin guidance for Q4 is cut below $33.0B / 79%, signaling HBM demand has peaked earlier than expected; OR NVDA Annual Meeting June 24 delivers a demand softening signal that reprices the entire AI hardware complex; OR DXY fails to clear 99.00 by June 24 AND the broader macro backdrop deteriorates (STEP_ASIDE scenario), removing support for adding semis longs in a hawkish-regime FOMC environment
targets: $156 — catalyst completion: MU reports Q3 above guidance ($33.5B+, GM 81%+, EPS $19.15+); sell-side begins upgrading MU from Hold to Buy; +10.2% from $141.5 entry midpoint; take 40% of position at this level

$185 — blue sky: full AI supercycle memory re-rating; MU valued at ~9.6x forward P/E on $19+ annualized EPS trajectory, implying the market is crediting a sustained 81%+ gross margin baseline rather than a cyclical peak; +30.8%; hold remaining 20% as long as quarterly earnings sustain the thesis
catalyst: Micron Q3 FY2026 earnings report scheduled after market close on June 24, 2026. Management guided record revenue of $33.5B (±$0.75B), gross margin ~81%, and non-GAAP EPS of $19.15 (±$0.40) — all near the all-time high for Micron. The same day, NVDA Annual Meeting of Stockholders (9 AM PT virtual) has Jensen Huang addressing AI demand trajectory, Taiwan $150B spending, and the $25B debt offering rationale. Two AI-semiconductor catalyst events on a single day create maximum volatility and upside optionality for the AI memory complex. SK Hynix's HBM4E sample confirmation for H2 2026 delivery provides additional read-through: if the next-generation product is also oversubscribed before launch, memory pricing power remains firmly with suppliers through at least mid-2027.
thesis:
Micron Q3 FY2026 arrives with management having guided record revenue of $33.5B — driven entirely by AI infrastructure and HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) demand that has structurally decoupled MU from the traditional DRAM commodity cycle. The AI capex confirmation cascade is extensive: NVDA's $25B bond offering generating $85B in orders, AMD's 57% YoY data center revenue growth in Q1, and every major hyperscaler reiterating or increasing compute capital expenditures for 2026. NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture requires approximately 8× HBM3E per GPU module, and with every GPU sold into data centers creating dedicated HBM demand, Micron and SK Hynix face structural supply deficits measured in quarters, not months.

The gross margin trajectory is the re-rating catalyst that the market has not yet fully credited. Management guided ~81% gross margin for Q3 — comparable to Qualcomm at peak. Memory companies historically trade at cyclical discounts because their margins swing between 10% and 60%+ with supply/demand conditions. At 81%, MU is demonstrating something the market has not priced since the pre-2022 era: HBM supply is genuinely capacity-constrained, and pricing power has shifted permanently from buyers (cloud hyperscalers) to suppliers (MU and SK Hynix). If this print confirms 81%+ and Q4 guidance implies sustained margins above 80%, the sell-side upgrade cycle accelerates — with approximately 15 analysts currently rated Hold on MU and only a handful at Buy, the upgrade catalyst is mathematical.

The June 24 double-event — MU earnings after close AND NVDA Annual Meeting at 9 AM PT — creates a compounding catalyst window. Jensen Huang's comments on AI demand trajectory, Taiwan production commitments, and post-$25B-debt-offering infrastructure plans will set the tone for the full AI hardware sector heading into MU's print. A constructive NVDA Annual Meeting raises all boats in the AI semis complex; a demand-softening signal at the NVDA meeting would be the worst-case scenario for MU shares even before the memory company reports. This is the primary reason the position is sized at 3% rather than 5% — the NVDA single-name event risk is embedded in the same trading day.

The counter-party is the memory bear who argues: (1) $33.5B quarterly revenue prices in perpetual AI capex growth with no digestion cycle — historical memory supercycles peak and reverse within 12–18 months as customers absorb inventory; (2) MU is a swing producer, and if NAND pricing stabilizes while DRAM demand plateaus in H2 2026, 81% is the cycle high, not a new floor; (3) SK Hynix's HBM4E confirmation means competition into H2 2026 is accelerating, potentially capping MU's pricing power into 2027. These are legitimate structural risks, which is why this is an event trade (1–2 week horizon), not a position trade (4–8 weeks), and the $128 stop reflects respect for the cyclical risk.
bull_case: MU reports Q3 revenue of $34.2B (beat by ~$700M), gross margin 82.5% (above the 81% guide), EPS $19.70. Q4 guidance: $35.5B–$36.0B, implying continued HBM demand acceleration and no inventory digestion concern. NVDA Annual Meeting same day: Jensen reiterates $200B+ AI infrastructure demand for calendar 2026. Sell-side upgrades begin the week of June 29: Goldman, Morgan Stanley, and BofA all move from Hold to Buy on MU. INTC's Apple foundry deal read-through adds credibility to the broader AI silicon supply chain narrative. MU reaches $155–160 within 5 sessions of the June 24 print.
bear_case: MU reports Q3 in line ($33.5B) but Q4 guidance disappoints: $32.0B–$33.0B and gross margin guiding to 78–79%, implying HBM pricing has plateaued. NVDA Annual Meeting shows Jensen noting 'demand remains strong but we are monitoring inventory levels at cloud customers' — a subtle softening signal. MU falls from $143 to $133–136 on the day-after reaction, approaching but not triggering the $128 stop. The position is held at 1/3 size pending further confirmation.
invalidation: $128 daily close; OR MU Q3 guidance implies gross margin below 79% for Q4 (memory price plateau); OR NVDA Annual Meeting Jensen delivers explicit demand softening language ('digestion period,' 'customer inventory build'); OR DXY fails to clear 99.00 by June 24 AND 30Y breaches 5.00% simultaneously (macro regime becomes actively hostile to all semi longs); OR SK Hynix or Samsung announces a significant increase in HBM3E capacity that would erode MU's pricing power within two quarters
